newsitem.title: UK: Dorling warns stg/dlr could hit 97 results.
newsitem.headline: Dorling warns stg/dlr could hit 97 results.

text.p: Book and CD-ROM publisher Dorling Kindersley Holdings Plc (DK) said on Tuesday that its 1997 turnover would be cut by five million stg and pre-tax profit by 1.6 million if the current pound/dollar rate were sustained.

"Were the current exchange rate of approximately $1.69 to the pound to be sustained for the rest of the financial year to June 1997, we estimate that this would reduce turnover and pre-tax profit by approximately five million stg and 1.6 million stg respectively," chairman and chief executive Peter Kindersley told shareholders at an annual general meeting.
"Since DK made its 1996 preliminary announcement in mid-September, sterling has appreciated by about nine percent," Kindersley said.

Current analyst forecasts are for 1997 pre-tax profit of some 21.0 million stg on sales of around 200 million stg. The company reported 1996 pre-tax profit of 17.4 million stg after generating turnover of 174.4 million stg.

Kindersley said DK was experiencing softer conditions in the U.S. book market after substantial growth in the past two years. But he added that book business was generally in line with expectations in the UK and in the rest of the world.

Trading conditions remained difficult for DK's multimedia division in the U.S. However, DK Multimedia is trading well in the UK and other areas and the division is expected to show good growth overall this year.
Kindersley said that DK will have its own sales force in the U.S. from January, selling only DK products and increasing sales focus in its largest market.
DK is set to publish under its own imprint in Australia from the third quarter of 1997 and expects sales there to increase significantly in due course.
"In summary, DK is a broadly based business in terms of media and geographical spread and, overall, the Directors anticipate that the Group will make progress in the current year," Kindersley said.
